items.text: Search lists for science stream career options mix three different questions into one.
Compare the four starting points below.

blocks.heading: Lead with the Lane Where Skill

items.text: We lead with the lane where skill, proof and a sale can grow income the furthest, then move to the lanes that need a planned business layer, and last to the lanes where success depends on winning stage after stage.
The skill sells as projects, consulting and products, and you set the pace.
How you enter: PCM, then B.Tech in computer science, or BSc in computer science, statistics or data science, or BCA.

blocks.heading: Skill Stack That Works in Every Lane

items.text: A degree opens a entry requirement.
Together these make a high-income skill portfolio, which is what lifts income ceilings.
The craft of your lane: code and statistics, a branch of engineering, patient care, pharmacy practice, lab method, or field and quality work.

blocks.heading: Years to First Pay
rows: B.Tech four years, or BSc three years (four-year honours is also offered under NEP), or BCA
Software engineer: Rs 5.37 lakh at entry level (414 salaries). Data analyst: Rs 4.13 lakh (576 salaries).
B.Tech four years, or diploma three years then B.Tech lateral entry for three more
Mechanical engineer: Rs 3.04 lakh at entry level (827 salaries).
Roughly four-year degrees, with registration or licence rules
Pharmacist: Rs 2.51 lakh at entry level (173 salaries).
BSc three years, MSc two more, often needed for research roles
Biotechnologist: Rs 4.92 lakh at entry level, but only 44 salaries, so treat it lightly.
Degree plus a quality, food-safety or sales skill
Food technologist: Rs 3.94 lakh at entry level (37 salaries, data last updated in July 2025).
BSc, MSc, then up to five years of JRF and SRF fellowship while you complete a PhD
Research scientist: Rs 6.08 lakh at entry level (48 salaries), a mix that may include PhD holders.

blocks.heading: College Cost Filter for Science Routes
rows: A government or low-fee BSc fits. Most private degrees sit past the caution line and need course-specific proof.
Good government and state-college seats fit. A costly private seat needs clear evidence of licence need, labs, internships and real placement outcomes.
A wider set of private seats fit. Keep the rest for living costs, exam attempts, tools and the second stage.

visuals.alt: A sequence outlines Five Rules for Choosing Between Lanes.
visuals.caption: Sequence of steps for Five Rules for Choosing Between Lanes.
visuals.heading: Five Rules for Choosing Between Lanes

items.text: "Science is the safe stream." Science gives range, not a result.
"The stream is the career." A stream is a key that fits some steps and not others.
"Respected means scalable." We rate each lane on how far skills, proof and a business layer can grow income, not on prestige.
Start from the lane, then work back to the stream.
Be strict before choosing PCB.
Use PCMB for a short delay, not as a plan.
Write a second route, whatever you choose.
Choosing the stream for the exam, not the lane.
Confusing safe with scalable.
Paying a large fee before checking approval.
A postgraduate degree to postpone the decision.
Treating one certificate as proof.
Debt for a vague path.
